title: Dabur India Ltd - 500096 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Dabur reiterates double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance after Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.6%, with India FMCG up 10.7%.
summary.overview: Dabur's India CEO Harjeet Bhalla presented a 18-month review of the seven-pillar vision, self-rating core brands and premiumisation as amber/green and M&A as red-to-be-revisited. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 11.6%, the second straight double-digit revenue quarter and fourth straight double-digit PAT quarter. India standalone grew 8.9%, with India FMCG up 10.7% (volume 5.5%, price 5.2%) and International growing about 20%. Management launched "Ignite" (four priorities: energise the core, execution, future-ready portfolio, savings) and said a medium-term plan to 2031 will come in the next six to eight months.

financial_highlights.change: second consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth
management says recovery started last quarter; not yet where it needs to be
operating profit impacted by supply chain, freight and logistics inflation at international level
up from 17% over 18 months; growing about 4x overall rate and margin accretive
distributor attrition down about 80%, throughput up 2x, distributor ROI up 30%

segments.name: India FMCG
segments.commentary: Grew 10.7% with volume 5.5% and pricing 5.2%; growth described as broad-based across segments.

segments.name: Home Personal Care (HPC)
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth despite input cost inflation; bulk of inflation mitigated in the quarter. Skin (Oxy, Gulabari) and home care (O'Donnell) flagged as growth areas.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Grew 6.9%. Chyawanprash and health supplements challenged; OTC and digestives (Hajmola, Pudin Hara, Hajmola-type brands) growing strong double digits; other healthcare portfolio in teens growth.

segments.name: Foods and Beverages (F&B)
segments.commentary: Foods growing strong double digits; beverages bounced back on a good season. Real active and 100% juices and coconut water growing strongly.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Growing about 20%, described as continuing strong momentum.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: Sustained strong double-digit growth; quick commerce seen as complementary for premium and innovation.

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Two quarters of mid-single-digit growth, with the quarter reportedly the highest GT growth in about 19 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Full-year revenue growth guidance reiterated at double digit; H1 delivered slightly ahead of that and management aims to sustain momentum in H2.
Ignite: invest an additional 150-200 bps of A&P (ad pro) in targeted consumer-facing brands, with disproportionate investment in OTC, digestives, skin care, home care and foods.
Premiumisation target raised to 23% of portfolio over the next 18 months, possibly sooner (from 20%).
Savings target: deliver 1.5x of the Rs 115 crore achieved during vision period; management cited about Rs 200 crore as an aspiration, while acknowledging the team's figure is lower.
Medium-term strategy plan to 2031 to be presented in the next six to eight months; full vision was due March 2028 but has been advanced.
Chyawanprash: strong winter loading done; new TVC and gummies format to drive relevance and usage through the next year.
Chemist channel program flagged as a key focus area for OTC and digestives.
Board inducted Harjeet Bhalla; no new global CEO planned; International business to continue to run independently under existing structure; Mr. Narang to provide oversight for other businesses.
capex_capacity: Capacity and capex not discussed in detail on the call.
Cessa (CESA) acquisition to be integrated into Dabur business from 1 December, with retrospective effect from 1 April.
Honey: Baddi (Himachal Pradesh) factory showcased; monofloral honey launch planned later in the month, priced at about 2.5x normal honey.
Retail Next program targeting about 40,000 stores; direct rural reach to expand to over 100,000 villages, geotagged.
Iris initiative launched for continuous replenishment (CRP) and forecasting accuracy to drive supply chain efficiencies.
demand_pricing: Input cost inflation elevated due to Middle East conflict and higher crude prices; HPC absorbed most inflation this quarter.
Price increases described as calibrated; portfolio mix and cost optimisation used to manage margins.
Chyawanprash: management acknowledges need to make the brand more relevant; new TVC and gummies format aimed at younger consumers.
Beverages: premium real active, 100% juices and coconut water gaining share; nectars core under pressure.
Quick commerce seen as complementary, enabling premium and more SKU lines than traditional GT.
Distributor consolidation (about 43% reduction) completed in about one year; management says no geographies were vacated and GT growth improved sequentially.
Digital media spend about 43% of total; influencers up over 3x with better efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of moving the M&A pillar from red to green in 18 months, and will the board back multiple real acquisitions? Also, plans for disruptive products and D2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to lock into an 18-month timeline; acquisitions must be adjacent to existing categories, strategic, synergistic and at the right valuation. D2C is nascent: a small Dabur shop, Sign by Dabur nutraceuticals brand, and higher-end CESA portfolio may be used to strengthen D2C.

qa_highlights.question: Can Chyawanprash shift gears after flat sales for 3-4 years; what about juices; and what about the group CEO structure and consultants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a TVC alone won't solve it; focus includes relevance messaging, gummies, strong winter loading and two-spoon usage. Beverages focus shifts to premium real and coconut water. No new global CEO; International runs independently; Mr. Narang oversees other businesses; the Mackenzie-supported strategy process decision on the consultant is pending.

qa_highlights.question: Did the 43% distributor reduction create white space, and how will the capital for growth investments be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidation was across separate foods, healthcare and HPC distribution systems and did not vacate geographies. Growth investments to be funded by efficiencies and mix/production gains; gross margin upside expected next fiscal from geopolitical developments; strong balance sheet for acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Should Dabur target 15-20% growth rather than double digit, and is the business under-invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not maintaining the status quo; certain pockets (OTC, digestives, skin, home care, premium) can deliver higher growth, but the company will not broad-brush a higher target. Investment is to be funded by efficiencies and sharper choices; no major people change needed.

qa_highlights.question: Where will incremental growth come from across HPC, foods and healthcare?
qa_highlights.answer: Health and wellness is the priority area, specifically OTC and digestives growing strongly, while health supplements remain challenged. F&B focuses on foods and premium beverages; HPC to sustain growth to fund investments; skin, home care (O'Donnell) and new categories like car and automatic diffusers are opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: How is the chemist channel being addressed given the healthcare focus?
qa_highlights.answer: Chemist program is part of Project Suction and a key focus for OTC and digestives, using MSL and digitisation to get the right portfolio into the right stores.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from elevated input and freight inflation; India standalone EBITDA dilution was only 10 bps but international operating profit was hit.
Healthcare growth at 6.9% with Chyawanprash and health supplements still challenged; recovery depends on winter loading and new communication.
M&A pillar rated red; timing, valuation discipline and category fit remain open questions.
A&P step-up of 150-200 bps depends on delivering efficiencies; management acknowledged media support fell short of vision commitments.
Mid-single-digit GT growth in previous two quarters; sustaining the step-up depends on the Retail Next and direct rural programs.
Medium-term 2031 plan due in six to eight months, which could bring a reset in targets.
Pending decision on the consultant for the strategy process.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution, the India FMCG recovery and guidance, but candid and self-critical on the vision scorecard (amber on core brand media and health and wellness, red on M&A). Management was evasive on M&A timing and on a higher growth ambition beyond double digit.
key_quotes: So right now I'm being tough on ourselves because we are getting solid growths from this portfolio, but it's the opportunity that we can look together if we were to put more focus in terms of investments in this space.
We are looking at doing an M&A if it meets with the strategic requirements of where Dabba is and where Dabba needs to get to.
It's not the reach that's important. It is what we are getting out of that reach that's going to be important.
And that's exactly why we are advancing our whole strategic exercise much earlier year and a half or so earlier than what we would do.

growth.why: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guidance was reiterated after Q2 consolidated revenue rose 11.6% and H1 ran slightly ahead of double digit, backed by pricing/mix, premiumisation and demand gains but no specific capacity or order numbers; capacity and capex were not discussed.

roles: Harjeet Bhalla (India CEO; inducted to Board)
mgmt.note: Harjeet Bhalla, India CEO, was inducted to the Board; he presented the 18-month vision review and Ignite growth priorities, with a medium-term plan to 2031 due in 6-8 months.
initiatives: Ignite: energise the core, execution, future-ready portfolio, savings
Extra 150-200 bps A&P in targeted consumer-facing brands
Premiumisation to 23% of portfolio within 18 months
Savings of 1.5x Rs 115 crore achieved during vision period

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is stepping up A&P by 150-200 bps and absorbing elevated input and freight inflation; India standalone gross margin diluted 10 bps and international operating profit was hit, with gross margin upside only expected next fiscal.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity and capex were not discussed in detail on the call; only the CESA integration from 1 December and the Baddi honey factory showcase were mentioned.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India FMCG volume grew 5.5% in Q2 with growth broad-based, GT grew mid-single digit for two quarters with the best GT quarter in about 19, and management aims to sustain H2 momentum behind a 150-200 bps A&P step-up.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; management said growth investments will be funded by efficiencies and mix/production gains rather than a stated capex plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue ran slightly ahead of double-digit guidance and management reiterated double digit for FY27, but it declined to raise the growth ambition beyond double digit and has elevated input-cost headwinds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input cost inflation from Middle East conflict and crude, plus freight and international profit pressure, could weigh on margins, and the 2031 medium-term plan due in 6-8 months could reset targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Monofloral honey launch is planned later in the month at about 2.5x normal honey price, Chyawanprash gummies and new TVC are rolling out through the next year, and D2C products like Sign by Dabur are being built.

rows.label: Project Samrithi savings to 1.5x of Rs 115 crore
rows.why: Management said it needs to deliver 1.5x the over Rs 115 crore achieved in the vision period, with Rs 200 crore cited as an aspiration, though the team's figure is lower.

rows.label: CESA acquisition integration
rows.why: The CESA acquisition is to be integrated into Dabur from 1 December, with retrospective effect from 1 April, adding a higher-end portfolio for D2C.

rows.label: Healthcare recovery and chemist channel push
rows.why: Healthcare grew only 6.9% with Chyawanprash and supplements challenged, while OTC and digestives grow strong double digits and a chemist program is a key focus, so recovery is not yet assured.

tone.note: Management was confident on India FMCG recovery and reiterated double-digit FY27 guidance, and candid on the vision scorecard (amber on core brands and health, red on M&A); analysts pushed on a higher growth ambition beyond double digit and the M&A timeline, which management avoided committing to.
